properties.company: OnTrack (New York, Susquehanna and Western Railway)
properties.speed_source: estimated for a slow-speed shared-track diesel railcar shuttle with frequent stops; unsourced. Note: despite being locally nicknamed like a streetcar service, OnTrack was not a true tram/light rail line -- it ran self-propelled 1950s Budd Rail Diesel Cars ('Buddliners') over a real freight railroad, the former Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Syracuse-Binghamton main line, sharing track with occasional freight moves.

segments.note: Conrail considered the ex-DL&W Syracuse-Binghamton line a financial burden and sold it for $1 to the Onondaga County Industrial Development Agency, which leased it to the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railway for both freight and a new passenger shuttle. OnTrack opened Sept 24 1994, using four Budd RDC-1 'Buddliners' from the 1950s. The core 'City Express' ran Carousel Center (now Destiny USA) - 600 Erie Place (flag stop) - Armory Square/Downtown - Syracuse University/Carrier Dome - Colvin Street; a seasonal summer-weekend extension continued via Rock Cut Road and Jamesville Village to Jamesville Beach Park, and special 'Orange Express' trains ran to Syracuse University football and basketball games at the Carrier Dome. Ridership started strong (45,757 riders in the first three months) but declined steadily over the following years despite roughly $8 million in cumulative state subsidy.
sources: VERIFIED 2026-08-24: "OnTrack was a suburban rail line that operated in Syracuse, New York, from 1994 to 2008. The line ran from the Carousel Center (today's Destiny USA) on the city's north side via Armory Square and Syracuse University to Colvin Street" — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OnTrack
Headway remains an estimate — the dates are verified, the service frequency is not.

segments.note: By 2007 daily ridership had fallen to around 50 passengers; regular City Express service ended in July 2007, leaving only weekend and Orange Express game-day trains. The final train ran in March 2008, ending the service permanently.
